Title: Project context and locked decisions (reference row)
Description:
Erdgut rewires three overlapping box-lifecycle models (Subscription->Box->Delivery, Order->Box->Delivery, Delivery+weekly-override gifting) into a single lineage. The audit found data drift on three axes: preferences live in 3 homes with no snapshot on boxes; address is chosen 3 different ways; status truth is split across 4 enums (OrderStatus, DeliveryStatus, BoxStatus, SubscriptionStatus). WeeklyBoxSetupService and TrialWeeklyBoxSetupService duplicate ~350 lines of distribution math.

LOCKED DECISIONS (do not revisit without explicit owner approval):
1. Trial Order stays as a thin shell, treated interchangeably downstream (NOT merged into Subscription).
2. PaymentMandate lives on User (survives cancel -> resubscribe).
3. Both pause window AND skip-set coexist; pause UI writes skip rows via SubscriptionSkipService (done in Phase 4).
4. Delivery weekday is zone-derived WITHIN one day; user picks preferred day and timeslot but admin can reschedule individual deliveries without cascading downstream weeks.
5. Cancellation notice is soft-disclaimed in copy (already done in P4.7). Admin handles exceptions manually.
6. First-class billing_mode enum: sumup_recurring | manual_invoice | manual_cash.
7. Preferences, allergies, and unit prices are SNAPSHOTTED on Box/BoxItem at compose time (simpler than versioning on Subscription).

MODEL CHANGES (Phase 1 backbone):
- NEW: payment_mandates (one per user, survives cancel)
- boxes gains: subscription_id FK, preferences_snapshot JSON, allergies_snapshot JSON
- box_items gains: unit_price_snapshot (historical receipts frozen)
- deliveries gains: box_id FK (kills fragile user+week join)
- subscriptions gains: address_id, delivery_weekday, preferred_timeslot, fulfillment_mode, billing_mode
- NEW: audit_events (replaces scattered Log::info; admin-visible history)
- NEW: subscription_skip_weeks (DONE in P4.4 — enables non-contiguous skips; pause window materializes into rows here)

PRODUCT CATALOG EXPANSION (from notes):
- products.allergens enum array (gluten, lactose, nuts, eggs, soy, fish, shellfish, celery, mustard, sesame, sulfites)
- products.dietary_tags enum array (vegan, vegetarian, contains_meat, contains_fish, contains_dairy)
- products.buying_price_cents (margin accessor)
- products.taste_profile enum array (sweet, earthy, fresh, peppery, umami, bitter, crisp, ...)
- products.pairings self-referential M2M ("goes well with")
- NEW: product_images (1..N per product, ordered)

COMPOSITION ENGINE:
WeeklyDistributionService (Phase 2) filters by user allergies + dietary prefs BEFORE distributing. Admin always has "force include anyway" override per item; warning chips in admin UI when forced item conflicts.

PLANNING HORIZON:
Config box_planner_weeks_ahead bumped to 12 (3 months). Admin weekly planner needs a compact multi-week grid view so 12 weeks doesn't overwhelm. Customer dashboard copy is already in place ("Orders and changes require a month's notice" — P4.7 done).

KNOWN BUGS TO FIX (folded into phase tickets):
- Trial pricing: Order::amount is computed once at checkout and pastes 35 EUR regardless of size/add-ons. Fix: BoxPricing::compute(size, addOns) shared service used by trial checkout AND subscription expected-charge.
- SumUp waiting state feels jarring in onboarding — redesign with reusable <x-payment.sumup-widget>.
- Emails often go to spam — SPF/DKIM/DMARC + transactional provider migration.
- Allergies stored as free text — move to enum-driven selector.

STRESS-TEST FLOWS (target: all 12 must pass at end of Phase 8):
1. Trial: signup -> pay -> delivered (works today)
2. Subscription recurring (no alignment today between charge date and composed week)
3. Subscribe during trial -> defer start (broken today — Phase 6)
4. Skip next week (works)
5. Skip non-contiguous weeks (DONE — P4.4)
6. Cancel with notice (soft disclaim only — DONE P4.7)
7. Change size mid-sub (works, copy done — P4.5)
8. Change allergies (works, copy done)
9. Switch to pickup (DONE — P4.1)
10. Egg add-on toggle (works; history line-item still TBD)
11. Change delivery weekday (broken — Phase 4.2)
12. Payment fails -> retry/pause (works, "mark paid externally" TBD — Phase 5-6)
13. Address changes apply to upcoming deliveries (DONE — P4.6)
14. Admin creates trial on behalf (Phase 5)
15. Admin creates subscription without SumUp cash/invoice (Phase 5)

RECOMMENDED SHIPPING ORDER:
Ship two small wins first — ERD-316 (SumUp widget) + ERD-336 (trial->sub defer) — before starting Phase 1 migrations. Each subsequent phase is independently deployable.
Acceptance Criteria: Reference only — not an implementation ticket. Do not close or mark Done.

Title: Per-user email history view in admin
Description:
Admins currently can't see which transactional emails have already been sent to a customer — only the resend action is audited. Add a chronological email-history section to the per-user admin page (/app/admin/users/{user}) so support can answer "did the customer get the trial confirmation?" / "why did they get two delivery reminders?" without grepping logs.

Capture every outbound email by listening to Illuminate\Mail\Events\MessageSent (or wrapping through a small EmailLogger service) and persisting one row per send. Reuse the existing `audit_events` table with `action='email_sent'`, or add a dedicated `email_log` table if `audit_events` becomes too noisy — decide once we measure volume.

Each row should carry: timestamp, mailable class (e.g. TrialOrderConfirmationMail), template/locale, recipient email at send time, related entity (order_id / box_id / subscription_id when known via Mailable metadata), delivery state (queued|sent|failed), and the actor when an admin triggered a resend (already wired via AdminEmailResendController). Bounce/complaint tracking can come later when we migrate provider (ERD-340).

UI: collapsible section on the user detail page with a paginated table — same density as the existing audit-timeline component. Filter by mailable class and date range. Optionally a per-row 'Erneut senden' button that points at the existing AdminEmailResendController flow.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every Mailable queued or sent for a user is recorded with timestamp, class, recipient, related entity, and delivery state.
- /app/admin/users/{user} shows an Email-Verlauf section listing the most recent N rows with pagination.
- Filter controls for mailable class and date range; default sort newest-first.
- Existing AdminEmailResendController resends still audit and now appear in the same history with actor.
- Feature test: triggering Mail::to(...)->queue(new TrialOrderConfirmationMail($order)) writes a row tied to the recipient user_id.
- Feature test: the admin user-detail page renders the Email-Verlauf section and lists the queued mailable.
- No PII leakage: only admin-authorised users may see the list (authorize('admin')).
